title: Preserve JSON boundaries in SSE fragmentation and fix delimiter coalescing
author: Maya Patel
description: Background: Several customers reported corrupted JSON objects when streaming structured outputs through our OpenAI-compat SSE bridge. Symptoms included truncated object boundaries when the runtime split tokens in the middle of JSON tokens, double delimiters when the transport concatenated small chunks, and occasional reordering when backpressure caused coalescing of intermediate frames. Root cause: The compatibility shim blindly concatenated incoming bytes into 'events' without tracking explicit JSON parse boundaries or emitted delimiter state. When partial JSON fragments were emitted as separate SSE 'data:' lines the consumer's streaming JSON parser could see an unterminated object (e.g. '{"choices": [ {"index": 0,' ) followed by a closing chunk later; in between, the shim sometimes collapsed adjacent delimiters into a single empty event which clients treated as an explicit 'done' marker. Changes in this PR: 1) Introduces an explicit fragment buffer for SSE events in the compat layer that tracks JSON structural state (curly/array nesting depth, string escape state) so we only emit a 'data:' event when a syntactic JSON boundary or an SSE max-chunk size threshold is reached. 2) Add a delimiter coalescing guard: we now collapse consecutive empty events into a single heartbeat event instead of emitting multiple delimiters. 3) For function/tool call messages we add a soft-boundary marker so the function payload (which can be large JSON) is emitted as single logical event even if it crosses tokenization boundaries. This avoids partial-function JSON delivered to tool runners. 4) Expose a feature-flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT) to opt into strict-json-boundary emission while we rollout. 5) New metrics: sse.fragmentation_count and sse.coalesced_delimiters to help detect regressions. 6) Added unit and integration tests including a fuzz harness that simulates arbitrary chunk boundaries and transport coalescing patterns. Testing and verification: - Unit tests for fragmenter edge cases including escaped quotes, unicode and nested arrays/objects. - Integration tests that run the OpenAI compatibility e2e harness with streaming clients (python and node) verifying valid incremental JSON frames. - Added a long-running perf canary that runs under canary infra for 24 hours to check latency/regression. - CI initially showed a flaky test (compat_sse_fuzz) which we fixed by making the harness deterministic for seed reuse; final CI green. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind the feature flag. - Enable OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT for Canary customers for 48h. - Monitor sse.fragmentation_count and sse.coalesced_delimiters; if fragmentation spikes, revert flag. - Gradual enable for 10% of traffic, then 50%, then global. Follow-ups: - Integrate this logic into dedicated runtime path (ENG-5065) to avoid duplication. - Add server-side sampling of partial-frame payloads (PII-safe) to aid debugging. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Metrics emitted - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Documentation note in compat README

release_notes: Fix: Prevents streamed JSON fragments from producing invalid partial objects in OpenAI-compat SSE streams.
Fix: Avoids duplicate SSE delimiters caused by transport coalescing which previously caused some clients to treat streams as complete.
Feature: OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_STRICT flag for strict JSON-boundary emission (off by default).
